 By Caroline Yaffa, WRAL state government reporter
 Election Day is over in North Carolina, but campaign signs are still lining roads and filling yards across the state. And if you don’t own the sign, or you're not authorized to remove it, you can’t just take it down.
 Here's what you need to know.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 How long can campaign signs stay up after an election? 
 Under state law, political signs placed along state-maintained roads must be removed within 10 days after an election. That means Friday, Nov. 13, this year.  The right-of-way time limits don’t apply to political signs on private property. 
 Can you remove someone else's campaign sign? 
 Not necessarily. If it’s your own sign, it is OK to remove it. But state law makes it a Class 3 misdemeanor to steal, deface, vandalize or unlawfully remove a compliant political sign that was lawfully placed by someone else. And authorities have prosecuted people accused of taking campaign signs.  
 What happens if campaign signs are left up too long? 
 Under state law, signs left on state-maintained roads for more than 30 additional days after the removal deadline, or Dec. 13 this year, are considered abandoned property. At that point, anyone can remove and dispose of them without penalty under the state's political sign law. The North Carolina Department of Transportation can also remove signs placed without authorization or left in state highway rights-of-way beyond the removal deadline.
 Deadline violations can be reported to a county board of elections or NCDOT.
